skill.name: computer-use-agents
skill.description: Build computer-use agents that can observe screens, reason about GUI state, and perform mouse, keyboard, shell, and text-editor actions. The skill focuses on sandboxed desktop automation patterns for Anthropic Computer Use, OpenAI CUA, and related vision-based agent systems.
skill.summary: Build sandboxed computer-use agents for GUI automation and screen-based workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation and sample code for computer-use agents, not an executable package. I confirmed the screen-capture and temporary screenshot handling risks because the examples capture display contents and store them in /tmp. Markdown code-fence detections, sandbox setup commands, and the role-token finding are false positives; no prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Screen capture examples can expose sensitive host data.
remediation.suggestion: Require an isolated desktop, scoped accounts, and explicit user consent before capturing or sending screenshots.

remediation.issue: Temporary screenshot files can leave sensitive images behind.
remediation.suggestion: Use private temporary files with restrictive permissions and delete screenshots immediately after processing.

remediation.issue: External screenshot commands depend on system tools.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command arguments hardcoded, avoid shell=True, check failures, and document sandbox prerequisites.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 237 is a normal from-import statement inside a documentation example, not a dynamic import() call. No runtime-loaded module path or user-controlled import is present.

The example invokes the external scrot binary to capture the display and write an image to /tmp. The command is hardcoded, but it is still a sensitive OS-level screen capture operation that requires sandboxing.
The detected text is a Markdown Python code-fence opener, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. It documents sample code and does not execute anything by itself.
The detected text is a Markdown code-fence closer, not command substitution. No shell command is being executed at this location.
The detected text is another Markdown Python code-fence opener. The backticks delimit documentation and are not shell execution.
The detected text is a Markdown code-fence closer after a Docker example. It is not Ruby or shell command execution.
The detected text is a Markdown Python code-fence opener before sample Anthropic code. It is not an executable backtick expression.
The Dockerfile RUN command creates a non-root container user for sandboxing. It is a controlled build instruction, not user-controlled shell execution.
The hidden .vnc directory is created inside the example container for virtual desktop configuration. It is not accessing host secrets or hidden user files.
Copying requirements.txt to /tmp occurs inside a Docker build example. This is temporary dependency staging, not sensitive file access.
Installing from /tmp/requirements.txt is part of the same Docker build example. It does not read private host data or accept dynamic file paths.
The example stores a screenshot at /tmp/screenshot.png after capturing the display. Temporary screenshot files can leak sensitive screen contents if permissions or cleanup are weak.
The example reads the captured screenshot back from /tmp/screenshot.png. This is expected for the workflow, but it handles sensitive screen data in a shared temporary path.

The skill presents screenshot capture as the core perception step for agents. This is a real sensitive capability because screenshots may include credentials or private data, even though the document recommends sandboxing.
The skill lists screenshot capture as a computer-use tool capability. This is legitimate for the domain but still creates high privacy risk if used outside an isolated environment.

Line 95 is an isolation checklist item saying filesystem access should be read-only or limited to temporary directories. It does not contain role-token text or instructions to override model behavior.

content.value_statement: Computer use agents need safe designs before they control screens, keyboards, and files. This skill provides implementation patterns, sandbox guidance, and Claude tool examples for safer GUI automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains perception, reasoning, and action loops for screen-based agents.
Shows Python examples for screenshots, mouse actions, keyboard input, and scrolling.
Describes Docker isolation, non-root users, restricted networks, and resource limits.
Outlines Anthropic Computer Use tools for screen, bash, and text editing workflows.
Highlights sharp edges such as UI reliability, cost control, and mandatory sandboxing.
limitations: The examples are partial and should not be copied without completion and review.
It does not provide a production-ready sandbox or deployment package.
It does not validate model outputs or tool inputs automatically.
It cannot make screen automation safe on an unsandboxed host.

use_cases.title: Prototype Desktop Agents
use_cases.description: Design the perception, reasoning, and action loop for a new GUI automation agent.

use_cases.title: Plan Safe Agent Sandboxes
use_cases.description: Map container, network, filesystem, credential, and resource controls before testing automation.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Computer Use Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare screen-based control risks with browser automation, APIs, and human review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Agent Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the perception, reasoning, action, and feedback loop for a computer-use agent. Include the main safety risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sandbox for a computer-use agent that needs browser access. Cover network, filesystem, credentials, and resource limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review An Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this computer-use workflow for unsafe screen capture, shell access, file access, and missing human approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production hardening checklist for a computer-use agent with screenshot tools, shell tools, and text editor tools.

output_examples.input: I need a safe architecture for a desktop automation agent.
output: A step-by-step agent loop with observation, planning, action, and feedback stages.
A sandbox checklist covering network limits, scoped files, credential isolation, and resource caps.
A list of approval points for screenshots, shell commands, and sensitive forms.

output_examples.input: Review my planned computer-use workflow before implementation.
output: A risk summary for screen capture, GUI actions, shell access, and file editing.
Specific safeguards such as non-root execution, private temporary files, and allowlisted endpoints.
Recommended tests for runaway loops, failed clicks, privacy leaks, and unexpected model actions.

best_practices: Run every computer-use agent inside an isolated desktop with no host credential access.
Keep screenshots, shell commands, and file edits behind explicit policy checks and logging.
Limit each run by time, steps, network destinations, filesystem scope, and human approval rules.
anti_patterns: Do not give a screen-control agent direct access to a personal workstation.
Do not store screenshots in shared temporary paths without cleanup and permission controls.
Do not let model-generated actions run shell commands without validation and allowlists.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design agents that observe screens and perform controlled GUI actions through mouse, keyboard, shell, and editor tools.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and partial examples that need review, completion, testing, and security hardening.

faq.question: Why is sandboxing required?
faq.answer: A computer-use agent can see private screen data and operate local tools, so host isolation limits damage.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful when planning computer-use workflows with Claude, Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools.

faq.question: What are the main security concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are screenshot privacy, shell access, file editing, credential exposure, and uncontrolled action loops.

faq.question: Should agents receive unrestricted internet access?
faq.answer: No. Network access should be limited to required endpoints and monitored during every run.
